findings.title: sp02_workspace_charge is flaky because three parallel tests share one process-global live-byte counter
findings.claim: The test binary replaces the global allocator and asserts on the difference of a global LIVE_BYTES counter around drop(ws); libtest runs the three tests concurrently, so allocations and frees of sibling tests fall inside the measurement window. It is a test-harness race, not a workspace accounting defect.
findings.evidence: crates/rodas5p-krylov/tests/sp02_workspace_charge.rs:20-21, 23-47, 49-54 (global allocator and counter), :100-102 and the same pattern at :155-157 and :214-216; no Mutex or serial guard in the file. research/production_loop_20261116/logs/baseline_facade_core_krylov.log:1007-1014: 'charged 20024 - released 14424 = 5600 > 640' and 'charged 20288 < released 4214311'. BASELINE_RESULTS.json flake_probe: 3/3 pass with --test-threads=1, 1 of 3 default runs fails.
findings.impact: Limits the baseline only: L-0300 FAIL is a harness artefact and says nothing about the solvers. production.yml runs this target with default threads, so hosted CI would fail intermittently. 35 test files in crates/*/tests use the same global-counter pattern and may share the hazard where a binary holds more than one measuring test (not checked).
findings.minimal_fix: Serialise the three tests with one static Mutex held for the whole test body, or count per thread with a thread_local counter in the allocator; the file is not protected.
